ai.literal: His heart to him belonging even after seeing, why, O my heart, you to us not belonging?
ai.translation: Even after seeing that his heart belongs only to him, O my heart, why is it that you do not belong to me?
ai.modern: அவருடைய நெஞ்சம் அவருக்கே உரியதாக இருப்பதை அறிந்தும், என் நெஞ்சமே! நீ எனக்கு ஆதரவாக இல்லாமல் இருப்பது ஏன்?
ai.explanation: The heroine is in a state of lovers' tiff and addresses her own heart with gentle frustration. She points out that her lover's heart is completely loyal to him, always guarding his feelings and interests. In contrast, her own heart does not stand by her; instead, it constantly sides with the lover and yearns for him. She questions why her own heart behaves like an outsider instead of being supportive of her.

ai.literal: Even at the moment of seeing him who does not love, thinking 'he will not be angry', you go, my heart.
ai.translation: O my heart! Even when you see him who does not show love, you still go to him, thinking that he will not be angry with you.
ai.modern: என்னிடம் அன்பு காட்டாதவரைப் பார்த்த போதிலும், 'அவர் கோபப்பட மாட்டார்' என்று நினைத்து அவரிடம் செல்கிறாயே, என் நெஞ்சமே!
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine addresses her own heart, which is eager to reunite with her distant lover. She points out the irony that even though he does not show affection ('uṟāatavar'), her heart immediately rushes to him the moment he is seen ('kaṇṭa kaṇṇum'). The heart foolishly reassures itself that he will not be angry or cold ('ceṟāar ena'). This portrays the helpless nature of love, where the heart ignores past indifference and remains ever-optimistic about the beloved.

ai.literal: To those who are ruined, friends do not exist, is it because of that saying, O heart, you, as desired, after him go?
ai.translation: O my heart! Is it because of the saying that those who are ruined have no friends, that you follow him as you please, leaving me behind?
ai.modern: நெஞ்சே! கெட்டவர்களுக்கு நண்பர்கள் இல்லை என்ற பழமொழி உண்மையோ? நீ உன் விருப்பப்படி என்னை விட்டுவிட்டு அவரிடமே செல்கிறாயே.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine addresses her own heart, which is eager to return to her lover despite his neglect. She asks if her heart is abandoning her because of the common proverb that 'those who are ruined have no friends' (கெட்டார்க்கு நட்டார் இல்). Here, 'கெட்டார்' (the ruined) refers to the heroine herself, who is wasted by the pain of separation. Her heart, which should act as her loyal friend ('நட்டார்'), is instead deserting her to go ('செலல்') after her lover according to its own desire ('பெட்டாங்கு'). This playful accusation highlights her helplessness and the conflict between her dignity and her desire.

ai.literal: Hereafter such things with you who will consult, O heart! Sulking having made, you do not enjoy, see, indeed!
ai.translation: O my heart! Who will consult with you hereafter on such matters? For you prolong your sulking and do not enjoy the pleasure of union when it is offered.
ai.modern: நெஞ்சமே! இனிமேல் உன்னோடு இது போன்ற காரியங்களை யார்தான் ஆலோசிப்பார்கள்? நீயோ ஊடல் செய்து இன்பத்தை அனுபவிக்காமல் விடுகிறாய், பார்!
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses their own heart in frustration. The heart had previously advised feigning anger (sulking) to heighten the pleasure of love, but when the opportunity for union arose, the heart prolonged the sulking and failed to enjoy the moment. The speaker declares that they will never consult their heart again on such matters. The phrase 'சூழ்வார் யார்' (who will consult?) emphasizes the loss of trust in one's own mind, while 'துனி செய்து துவ்வாய்' (having sulked, you do not enjoy) highlights the self-defeating nature of the heart's advice.

ai.literal: Not obtaining fears; if obtained, separation fears; unending affliction-natured is my heart.
ai.translation: My heart is possessed of unending affliction: it fears when it does not obtain union, and if it does obtain it, it fears separation.
ai.modern: என் நெஞ்சம் எப்போதும் நீங்காத துன்பத்தை உடையதாக இருக்கிறது; காதலரைப் பெறாதபோது பெறவில்லையே என்று அஞ்சுகிறது, பெற்றுவிட்டால் பிரிந்துவிடுவாரோ என்று அஞ்சுகிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet portrays the constant state of anxiety experienced by a lover's heart. When the lover is absent, the heart is filled with fear that it will never achieve union. However, even when union is achieved, the heart cannot rejoice fully because it immediately begins to fear the pain of future separation. Through the words 'peṟāamai añcum' (fears not obtaining) and 'peṟiṉ pirivu añcum' (if obtained, fears separation), the poet shows how the heart is trapped in a loop of worry, making its sorrow truly 'aṟāa iṭumpai' (ceaseless affliction).

ai.literal: When staying alone and thinking, my heart was there to devour me.
ai.translation: When I remain all alone and think of him, my own heart is poised to devour me.
ai.modern: நான் தனியாக இருந்து அவரைப் பற்றி நினைக்கும் போது, என் நெஞ்சு என்னை விழுங்குவது போல் வருத்துவதாக இருந்தது.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine describes the agonizing pain of separation. When she is left entirely alone and begins to contemplate her lover, her own heart does not offer comfort; instead, it turns against her. The word 'tiṉiya' (to eat or devour) vividly illustrates how her inner thoughts and longing feel like a physical force consuming her from within. She expostulates with her heart because its constant dwelling on the beloved acts as a self-destructive torment.

ai.literal: Even modesty I forgot, him to forget unable my unworthy foolish heart by being caught.
ai.translation: Caught in my unworthy, foolish heart that is utterly unable to forget him, I have forgotten even my own modesty.
ai.modern: அவரை மறக்க முடியாத என்னுடைய தகுதியற்ற அறிவற்ற நெஞ்சத்தின் வசப்பட்டதால், நான் என் நாணத்தையும் மறந்துவிட்டேன்.
ai.explanation: The heroine laments her loss of self-control and modesty. She describes her heart as unworthy (மாணா) and foolish (மட) because it stubbornly refuses to forget her lover, despite his behavior. Being trapped (பட்டு) by the dictates of this relentless heart, she confesses that she has lost her sense of reserve and forgotten even her modesty (நாணும் மறந்தேன்).

ai.literal: If [I] despise [him], it will be a disgrace, thinking thus, my life-loving heart thinks of his virtues.
ai.translation: Thinking that it would be a disgrace to despise him, my life-loving heart thinks only of his virtues.
ai.modern: அவரை இகழ்ந்து பேசினால் அது நமக்கு இழிவாகும் என்று நினைத்து, என் உயிர் மேல் ஆசை கொண்ட நெஞ்சம் அவருடைய நற்குணங்களையே நினைத்துப் பார்க்கிறது.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine speaks of her heart's inability to stay angry with her beloved. She notes that if she were to despise or blame him for his absence, it would only bring disgrace to their love. To avoid this humiliation and to preserve its own life, her heart, which is deeply attached to living, chooses to focus entirely on his good qualities. The phrase 'uyirkkātal neñcu' highlights how the heart clings to life by choosing love and positive remembrance over resentment.

ai.literal: To suffering who indeed companion will become, one's own heart companion not being when?
ai.translation: Who indeed will stand as a companion in times of grief, if one's own heart does not act as a support?
ai.modern: தம்முடைய நெஞ்சமே தமக்குத் துணையாக இல்லாதபோது, துன்பம் வரும்போது வேறு யார் துணையாக இருப்பார்கள்?
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the speaker laments the lack of inner strength and support from their own mind during a period of intense love-sickness. The key phrase 'துணையல் வழி' combines 'துணை' (support), 'அல்' (not), and 'வழி' (when/in the event of), meaning 'when it is not a support'. The poet argues that if one's own 'நெஞ்சம்' (heart/mind) deserts them and refuses to offer comfort, it is completely futile to expect any external companion ('யாரே துணை ஆவார்') to help ease the suffering.

ai.literal: Naturally, strangers are not one's own people, when one's own possessing heart is not friendly.
ai.translation: It is only natural that strangers do not act as our friends, when our very own heart does not stand by us.
ai.modern: நம்முடைய சொந்த நெஞ்சமே நமக்குத் துணையாக இல்லாதபோது, அயலார் நமக்கு உறவினராக இல்லாமல் இருப்பது இயல்பானதே.
ai.explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments the behavior of her own heart, which constantly sides with her lover instead of supporting her. She reasons that when one's own heart (neñcam) does not act as a loyal friend (tamar al vaḻi), it is completely natural (tañcam) that strangers (ētilār) do not show any friendliness (tamar allar) either. The word 'tañcam' is used here in the sense of 'easy' or 'no wonder', emphasizing that internal betrayal makes external indifference entirely expected. This poignant observation highlights the deep internal conflict of a lover whose mind refuses to cooperate with her resolve.
